plans.title: Visuals in the chat
plans.goal: Agent sessions, build sessions especially, should show rich visuals in the chat: flow diagrams and maps of the parts a change touches, drawn with our own design system. That needs an architecture decision, the design system’s components, the transcript designed in Design Workspace, Fix Something and Build, and then built.
plans.brief:
Agent sessions, build sessions especially, show rich visuals in the chat: flow diagrams and maps of the parts a change touches, drawn with the design system’s own components.

The agent never writes HTML into the chat. A visual is a fenced block in a small, versioned vocabulary that Prelude parses, checks (part ids must exist) and renders with a design-system partial. Anything it can’t read stays a plain code block, as the agent wrote it.

Ask and fix conversations use the same transcript, so whatever a design session shows, they show too.

activity.says: The agent drafted 8 steps from your goal. It added Fix Something’s build, which no other step covered.

steps.title: Prelude Architecture
steps.doneWhen: Its decision is proposed, you’ve agreed it, and it’s merged into main.
steps.prompt:
Propose a decision for how rich visuals in agent sessions fit the architecture. Discuss it with me before writing anything.

Decide with me which part parses and renders visuals (views, or a new part); how the vocabulary is versioned, and how agents are told it (agent.js); and where it happens in the turn flow (flows/turn.md): at save time or at render time.

Before proposing, check how Koda’s renderMarkdown handles a fenced block’s language tag, since that decides whether blocks are pulled out before rendering or after. Then write the proposed decision, any new or changed part, and a flow “A visual in a message”.

Ask and fix conversations use the same transcript. askPrompt gets no architecture brief today: decide whether it should. The vocabulary goes into askPrompt and fixPrompt too.

steps.title: Prelude Design System
steps.doneWhen: Its screens are approved and it’s merged into main.
steps.prompt:
Support rich visuals in agent chats, starting with flow diagrams and maps of the parts a change touches.

1. Series colours. Bring --series-* back in tokens.css (ds/v1 had five), named by role if a better name fits, in both themes, and show them on the tokens screen. Add to guideline 3: series colours tell things apart, never mean good, warn or danger, and always have a label.

2. A flow component: a flow’s steps through the parts that do them, a column per part and a row per step, with what passes between them. No script; it has to fit a chat column, so use container queries. And two markers on the map: touched in this change, and would change. Each says which in words.

3. A guideline for rich components, so every stack builds them the same way: the component’s HTML file is the contract, each stack renders it from a model with one partial, script only for what’s truly imperative, no custom elements except a host’s renderers. Update the gallery in the same turn.
